name: Cult of personality
scope: The cult of personality as the sources define it: a deliberately built system of art, symbolism and ritual that glorifies one individual in quasi-religious terms, above all the modern political leader cult (a state or party using mass media to enforce the leader's power, magnify their ideology and legitimise their rule), with its ancient and early modern antecedents (Britannica) and the Soviet leader cult from Lenin to Brezhnev (Encyclopedia of Russian History). Texts: Khrushchev's 1956 Secret Speech and the Stalin-era Short Course. Excludes celebrity or fan worship, the use of the phrase merely as an accusation, and the particular ideologies (fascism, Stalinism, Maoism) that the cults served.

summary: A cult of personality is a deliberately built system of art, symbolism and ritual that glorifies one individual in quasi-religious terms. In its modern political form a state or party uses mass media, propaganda and ritual displays of loyalty to enforce the leader's power, magnify their ideology and legitimise their rule. The sources describe the practice and its history; they record no programme beyond the glorification itself, and critics (Khrushchev, scholars) treat it as an abuse.
